commit_subject: (screen-flagged) b1.6 generalize (PR #1300): decouples component gates from exemplar flags; PR body says the witness's exemplar coupling "unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins" — logic/scope correction to 100 merged generated modules.
description: never again zeroed by China-list or aluminum membership (the witness's exemplar coupling, which round-2 evaluation showed unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins)

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The §122 surcharge exemption branch fired on the witness's exemplar-line identity flags (entry_is_line_a, a China-301 list-1 exemplar, or entry_is_line_b, an aluminum exemplar) rather than on the source's actual exceptions, so at schedule scale every China-301-listed line was zeroed out of the 10% temporary import surcharge for all origins while §232-covered steel/copper lines that were not the aluminum exemplar were surcharged.
triage.triage_notes: Generated chapter composition (module.kind: composition), rulespec/v1, 158-line diff; indices 96-99 all received the identical hunk shape. Six component gates were re-grounded: section_122_component_rate (entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b -> entry_is_section_122_exempt or entry_is_section_232_covered; that rule's own proof atoms cite the 9903.03.03 subdivision (aa)(ii) exclusion list and 'articles of aluminum, of steel, or of copper or derivative aluminum or steel articles provided for in headings 9903.82.02 and 9903.82.04' as the exceptions, which the new predicates match and the old exemplar flags did not); section_232_aluminum_component_rate (both versions, line_b -> entry_is_section_232_aluminum); china_section_301_component_rate (line_a/b/c/e -> list123 / 2024_action / list4a / solar, while entry_is_line_d is deliberately retained per the summary 'Beer/section-338 keeps entry_is_line_d because no membership module exists'); brazil_section_301_component_rate and forced_labor_section_301_component_rate, where the pre-fix formulas applied the duty to EVERY entry of a covered origin except the line_a/line_b exemplars and the fix narrows them to entry_is_brazil_301_listed / entry_is_forced_labor_301_listed (an additional over-application defect in the same hunk). section_201_component_rate's rename (line_e -> entry_is_section_201_cspv) is a runtime no-op because both branches are 0. SECOND FIDELITY CHANGE in the same module: a previously absent §232 steel duty is added (ch98_s232_steel_heading_rate = '0.50' and section_232_steel_component_rate, atoms citing us/statute/hts/9903.81.87 and .88, excerpt 'Rates of duty (1-General): The duty provided in the applicable subheading + 50%') and summed into schedule_statutory_stack - that half is unrepresented_clause; I coded the module's decisive kind from the §122 gate the PR headlines. Kind call is contestable: wrong_entity_or_scope is a defensible alternative since the wrongly-gated rule hit the wrong population; I chose untraceable_branch because the exemplar-flag predicate has no basis in the cited source at all and the fix re-grounds it. Provision text could NOT be read: resolve_provision.py returned {"error": "unresolved"} for us/statute/hts/9903.81.87 ("Corpus descendants for 'us/statute/hts' cross active release scopes"), so the source check rests on the modules' own proof-atom excerpts plus the PR body. Also in the diff and NOT defects: the module summary prose was rewritten (generator b1.6-schedule-compositions-2 -> -3) and a ch98-prefixed scalar rename (s232_steel_heading_rate -> ch98_s232_steel_heading_rate) was recorded. Caveat for reviewers: this commit is a pre-repair snapshot of PR #1300 - the added section_232_steel_component_rate here carries double-nested metadata.proof.proof.atoms and cites 9903.81.87/.88, while the PR body says the rate is 'grounded on the consolidated HTS 9903.82.02 provision' and the PR issue comment records a later repair ('steel atoms unwrapped to canonical metadata.proof.atoms'; '9903.82.02 provision added to every module's source-verification set'); a9562cfd44 is not an ancestor of the local HEAD so I could not see the repair commits. Companion test files for all four chapters also changed (they feed the new membership inputs).
triage.verifier_justification: The §122 exemption branch is the only condition in `rules[section_122_component_rate].versions[1].formula`, and the fix replaces two witness-fixture line-identity flags with the two exception classes the rule's own unchanged proof atoms cite — `kind: exception` atoms for `subdivision (aa)(ii) exclusion list under heading 9903.03.03`, excerpt `7202.11.10`, and excerpt `articles of aluminum, of steel, or of copper or derivative aluminum or steel articles provided for in headings 9903.82.02 and 9903.82.04` — so the source claim stayed constant while the encoded condition moved onto it, which is re-grounding an untraceable condition, not added coverage. `tools/b16_entry_flags.py` at the fix commit proves the pre-fix condition had no source basis: `entry_is_line_a` is literally `hts == "7202111000"` while the new `entry_is_section_122_exempt` reads the `s122_aa_ii/aa_iii` membership tables and `entry_is_section_232_covered` the §232 aluminum/steel tables. The refutation that these were merely opaque caller inputs fails because the same `entry_is_line_a` flag simultaneously served as the §301 list-1 condition in `china_section_301_component_rate` and as the §122 exclusion condition — two provably different line sets, so no assignment could satisfy both cited provisions, and the PR body independently calls the pre-fix behavior one that "unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins."
triage.verifier_notes: Kept the first reader's kind after trying to break it. (1) "not_a_defect / new coverage" fails: the pre-fix rule already carried `kind: exception` proof atoms for the (aa)(ii) exclusion list and the §232 aluminum/steel/copper exclusion on the very formula path being changed, so the module did claim to encode those exceptions and encoded them as exemplar identity instead. (2) "mechanical" fails: a formula token inside an effective-dated version changed; atoms, dates, dtype, entity and outputs are byte-identical pre→post. (3) Alternative kind wrong_entity_or_scope is arguable (the exemption reached the wrong population of lines in both directions — all §301 list-1/2/3 lines wrongly exempted, §232 steel/copper lines wrongly surcharged), but the rule's entity, period and output surface are unchanged; the defect is a branch condition with no source basis that the fix re-grounds, which the taxonomy assigns to untraceable_branch. Reviewer caveats: the same commit also does two things that are NOT this kind and should not be folded into this case — it adds a brand-new `section_232_steel_component_rate` rule plus `ch98_s232_steel_heading_rate` wired into `schedule_statutory_stack` (closer to unrepresented_clause, or arguably new coverage the witness never claimed since the PR says its steel exemplar 7202.11.10.00 sits outside note 16(c)), and it adds missing `entry_is_brazil_301_listed` / `entry_is_forced_labor_301_listed` membership conditions to the Brazil and forced-labor components (unrepresented_clause flavor: pre-fix those rates applied to every Brazil-origin / listed-origin line regardless of list membership). Source-text confirmation through the pinned release is inconclusive by itself: the corpus pin resolves to HTS 2026 Rev. 3, where `chapter-99/page-221` and `page-230` carry note 16 steel text rather than the §122 heading 9903.03.01/.03 subchapter notes the atoms excerpt (page numbering shifted between revisions), so the determination rests on the diff, the module's own atoms, the flag tool, and the PR body. Worth noting page-221 under the pin does show the schedule's standard exclusion idiom ("The additional duties imposed by heading 9903.01.77 shall not apply to ... articles provided for in headings ..."), i.e. heading-membership predicates, never per-line exemplar identity.
